title: Verdict, 2026-09-01 (baseline)
preamble: Baseline verdict after initial synthetic Zipfian benchmark (E1).

verdicts.headline: Predicted 45% fewer primary DB reads on synthetic skew
verdicts.summary: Predicted to cut primary read QPS by 45% against stock Postgres (B0) under assumed Zipf(0.99) skew.

verdicts.headline: Zero-code SQL wire proxy pitch
verdicts.summary: Drop-in wire proxy requires no application changes, conditional on safe invalidation.

verdicts.headline: Postgres performance audits can fund development
verdicts.summary: Fixed-scope query-bottleneck audits if >=3 teams sign by Q4.

verdicts.headline: Crowded managed-Postgres space; needs real workload replay
verdicts.summary: Needs E2 evidence on real multi-tenant write-heavy traces before pitching seed investors.

scorecard.reasoning: 45% lower read load predicted under synthetic Zipfian workload.
Within 4% of hand-tuned Redis read-aside in synthetic tests.
Wire-protocol parser handles simple SELECTs only; prepared statements unbuilt.
Managed RDS/CloudSQL bills scale with read replicas.
Automatic WAL-based invalidation is the proposed wedge, not yet tested.

strengths.text: No application code edits required compared with manual Redis cache-aside (structural deployment difference).

risks.risk: Real SaaS workloads write too frequently for table-level invalidation
risks.kill_criterion: Hit rate below 20% on two real multi-tenant SQL traces

risks.risk: No team trusts an inline proxy in front of production Postgres
risks.kill_criterion: Fewer than 2 teams agree to a shadow-mode replay

next_tests.title: Replay two public multi-tenant SQL traces (E1 -> E2, 6 hours)
next_tests.detail: Compare hit rate and staleness against tuned Redis TTL.
next_tests.outcome: Ran 2026-09-18: ML prefetcher failed; row-key invalidation held 31% hit rate.

title: Verdict, 2026-10-01
preamble: Second verdict after replaying two anonymized SaaS SQL traces (E2) and holding 6 operator interviews.

verdicts.headline: 31% read offload on real traces vs B0; ML prefetcher dropped
verdicts.summary: Row-level WAL invalidation is predicted to offload 28–34% of reads on two real traces against B0, but matches tuned Redis (B1). ML prefetcher dropped after adding <1% hit rate.

verdicts.headline: Verify & shadow-audit CLI first; inline proxy blocked by trust
verdicts.summary: Five of six operators refused an inline proxy before seeing a zero-risk shadow report on their own query log. Ship offline log analyzer + shadow verifier first.

verdicts.headline: 2 paid trace assessments booked
verdicts.summary: Two SaaS teams agreed to fixed-price query-offload assessments from exported logs.

verdicts.headline: No algorithmic moat over Redis once hotspots are identified
verdicts.summary: Once the report identifies the 12 hot queries, teams cache them in existing Redis in a day. Revisit only if live WAL invalidation proves indispensable in E3.

disconfirming.text: ML query-prefetcher dropped under pre-stated rule: added +0.6% hit rate (<5% bar) at 3x memory overhead.
Inline proxy rejected on trust grounds by 5 of 6 interviewed operators prior to shadow proof.
Against tuned Redis on the top 15 queries (B1), net DB CPU difference is predicted within 2%.

confirming.text: Row-level WAL invalidation cleared the 20% hit-rate bar on both write-heavy traces (28% and 34%).
Two operators offered exported pg_stat_statements + WAL logs for a paid diagnostic report.

killed_or_failed.rule_and_finding: +0.6% hit-rate gain over LRU on two production traces, below the pre-stated 5% threshold.

scorecard.reasoning: 28–34% primary read reduction predicted on two real multi-tenant traces.
Caching top 15 queries in existing Redis captures ~90% of the same offload.
Offline log analyzer needs zero inline privileges; proxy deferred.
Teams pay for diagnosis and verification, reluctant to install inline proxy.
Wedge is exact WAL-aware staleness accounting, not raw cache throughput.

outside_review.summary: No independent human check of the trace replay yet.

strengths.text: Exact WAL-invalidated counterfactual replay on real query + write logs (E2).
Pre-stated 5% rule killed the ML prefetcher before building runtime complexity.

risks.risk: Teams fix top queries once and churn
risks.kill_criterion: Zero repeat or monitoring engagements from first 3 assessment clients
Predicted offload differs from first live E3 pilot by >25%

next_tests.title: Run first paid log assessment + measure before/after replica CPU (E2 -> E3)
next_tests.detail: Tests whether offline prediction matches live traffic once top queries are cached.

contradictions.proposal: Move offline trace report ahead of wire-protocol proxy.
